target_customer: Hospital and health system pharmacy departments that need answers to clinical questions from physicians
problem: Hospital clinical pharmacists spend large amounts of time researching drug information questions; InpharmD outsources this with AI plus pharmacist review.
business_model: B2B subscription service per health system for outsourced drug information answers

founders.name: Ashish Advani
founders.background_notes: About 10 years as a clinical pharmacist focused on drug information and about 10 years running a drug information center, per the YC page.

founders.name: Tulasee Rao Chintha
education: Bachelor of Technology, Jawaharlal Nehru Technological University
founders.background_notes: Full-stack software architect per the YC page.

competitors.name: Lexicomp and Micromedex
competitors.what: Subscription clinical drug reference databases that hospital pharmacists searched themselves; no outsourced answer service
competitors.traction_then: Dominant reference tools in hospitals, per a pharmacist database survey
competitors.funding_then: Owned by Wolters Kluwer and IBM, not venture funded

technical_complexity.rationale: Literature search plus a pharmacist review workflow was standard engineering in 2021; the AI layer arrived later with GPT-3 era models.

defensibility.rationale: A curated library of answered questions and pharmacist network plus health system relationships, but the underlying literature is public.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found showing incumbents copying the outsourced model; the company site compares its answers with generic GPT output and names UpToDate as a manual tool.

market_need_then: Hospitals employ clinical pharmacists to answer physician questions and the company states it saves pharmacist hours; the YC pitch says hospitals outsource this because it is more efficient.

identity.logo: Wordmark with a trademark symbol on the site

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand, no community or merch found; a blend of Inpharm and D that reads as a pharma term, functional but not iconic.

outcome_analysis: InpharmD is active and reported as profitable at its December 2023 seed, which was its first announced institutional round, led by 645 Ventures. A pharmacist founder paired with an engineer fits the niche, and growth came from selling to health systems rather than burning cash. The company site claims more than 30 health systems, but this is self reported. No acquisition, layoff or shutdown news was found.
notes: Seed figure is $6.05M per company post and Lowenstein; the company's Exclusive post says $6M and aggregators say $6.1M to $6.5M. Competitor source is an undated survey, so source_date is null. Aggregators list earlier small rounds (CB Insights total $6.18M over 3 rounds) that were not verified.
